simple.meaning: מָצוֹק (mâtsôwq) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a narrow place , i.e. (abstractly and figuratively) confinement or disability.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H4689. matsoq מָצוֺק noun [masculine] straitness, straits, stress ; — always absolute ׳מ ; — מ ׳כָּלאִֿישׁ 1Sam 22:2 every man of straits (in straits); וּבְמ ׳בְּמָצוֺר Deut 28:53 , 55 , 57 ; Jer 19:9 (all of national straits ); ׳צַרוּֿמ מְצָאוּנִי Psa 119:143 ; perhaps read מָצוֺק also 32:6 , for רק מצא , compare Du Br.
